claim: arch_impact_classifier.md's `## Interface` section fixes Classify's signature at two inputs with no failure mode ('One call, taking the diff's changes together with a map from module identity hash to module name. ... has no failure mode'), and arch_diff_command.md's Responsibilities list hands ImpactClassifier exactly those two things ('Hand that list and that map to ImpactClassifier and take back the same list with a level on each entry') with no step anywhere in DiffCommand's Responsibilities or Interface that resolves a profile or handles a profile-resolution failure. Yet the same arch_impact_classifier.md (Impact Levels section) and module.json's requirement 425146f32e96 both require the node-type-to-level mapping to be read from 'the resolved profile', and test_diff_classification.md S15 asserts `Classify` must actually apply a project's `spec/profile.json` declarations.
authoritative_source: The case is undecided: no leaf says how the resolved profile is meant to travel from disk into Classify's per-change decision. schema.ResolveProfile(specDir) is the only existing way to obtain a profile and it both touches the filesystem and returns an error — incompatible with a Classify that takes no spec directory and 'has no failure mode' per its own Interface section. TreeBuilder (arch_tree_builder.md) sets a precedent for the alternative — BuildTree takes the specDir itself, calls schema.ResolveProfile internally, and surfaces the error through its own existing failure mode — but arch_diff_command.md's Responsibilities never asks DiffCommand to resolve a profile or forward one to ImpactClassifier, and arch_impact_classifier.md never gives Classify a specDir parameter or a failure mode to report a broken profile.json through.
evidence: This PR (commit 56ed694) resolved the contradiction by adding an optional variadic `profile ...*schema.Profile` parameter to Classify, defaulting to schema.DefaultProfile() when omitted, so every existing call site keeps compiling unchanged. But the classifier's only production call site, cmd/spex/diff.go:67 (`merkle.Classify(changes, moduleNames)`), never supplies a profile and arch_diff_command.md gives DiffCommand no instruction to resolve or pass one — so in a project carrying spec/profile.json, `spex diff` always classifies against schema.DefaultProfile() and reports `unknown` for every profile-declared type. Requirement 425146f32e96's profile-driven mapping is therefore only exercised by merkle/impact_classifier_test.go's direct calls to Classify with an explicit profile argument (S15), never by the product. The two leaves genuinely conflict on call arity and failure mode, and neither leaf nor any other in this bead's scope decides which one yields — this is the bead's own contract, and it is unimplementable as written without picking a side no leaf licenses.
proposed_fix: Make the profile a required, non-variadic third argument to Classify (`Classify(changes []Change, moduleNames map[string]string, profile *schema.Profile) []ClassifiedChange`), and update arch_diff_command.md's Responsibilities to insert a profile-resolution step before 'Hand that list and that map to ImpactClassifier' — DiffCommand resolves the profile via schema.ResolveProfile(specDir) alongside (or instead of) TreeBuilder's existing internal call, surfaces a resolution failure through the same pre-flight-style error/exit-code path runDiffE already uses for other setup failures, and hands 'that list, that map, and that profile' to ImpactClassifier. Update arch_impact_classifier.md's Interface section to state the three-input, still-failure-free signature (Classify itself still cannot fail; only resolving the profile can) so the two leaves agree.
